description: Texas-specific deduction categories grounded in Tex. Prop. Code §92.104.

deduction_categories.name: Cleaning
deduction_categories.permissible_when: Cleaning is required due to tenant-caused conditions beyond normal wear.
deduction_categories.not_permissible_when: Normal accumulation of dust/dirt; cleaning that constitutes normal wear and tear; unit was not clean at move-in.
deduction_categories.typical_rebuttal: Under Tex. Prop. Code §92.104(a), a landlord may not retain any portion of the security deposit to cover normal wear and tear. Tenants in similar situations in Texas typically note that basic cleaning after a tenancy constitutes normal wear and tear.

deduction_categories.name: Painting / Wall Repair
deduction_categories.permissible_when: Tenant caused damage beyond normal wear — large holes, unauthorized colors, significant damage.
deduction_categories.not_permissible_when: Normal wear: nail holes, faded paint, minor scuffs after reasonable tenancy.
deduction_categories.typical_rebuttal: Under Tex. Prop. Code §92.104(a), normal wear and tear is not deductible. Tenants in Texas in similar circumstances typically note that minor nail holes, faded paint, and normal scuffs after a {{tenancy_years}}-year tenancy are normal wear and tear.

deduction_categories.name: Carpet / Flooring
deduction_categories.permissible_when: Tenant caused damage beyond normal wear — burns, large stains, pet damage.
deduction_categories.not_permissible_when: Normal wear patterns, matting, minor stains. Must account for useful life depreciation.
deduction_categories.typical_rebuttal: Normal carpet wear from regular use is not deductible under Tex. Prop. Code §92.104(a). Tenants in similar situations note that carpet has a useful life and replacement costs should be prorated based on the carpet's age.

deduction_categories.name: Failure to Provide Itemized Statement
deduction_categories.permissible_when: Never — itemization is always required when deductions are made.
deduction_categories.not_permissible_when: Landlord retains any portion without providing written itemized list.
deduction_categories.typical_rebuttal: Under Tex. Prop. Code §92.104(b), a landlord who retains any portion of the security deposit must provide the tenant with a written description and itemized list of all deductions. The failure to provide this itemization may constitute bad faith retention under §92.109.
evidence_helpful: Absence of itemization is the evidence
